questions_used.question: How separate are the OOB and in-band worlds?
questions_used.answer: Completely. OOB is its own Ethernet network for hardware control; the in-band fabric carries training and storage. Keep the two worlds apart so nothing reads across them.

questions_used.question: The OOB fan: one line per BMC, or one trunk?
questions_used.answer: One trunk that splits exactly once into the compute BMC, NVSwitch BMC and power shelf branches. Not a pile of lines that happen to touch.

questions_used.question: Free software only?
questions_used.answer: Yes. Anything that needs money stays out, and don't imply the gated images are free.

questions_used.question: Panes, or a canvas?
questions_used.answer: One canvas with a diagram per world is fine if that keeps the planes from bleeding into each other.

questions_used.question: How is oob -> nvos drawn when the canvas form cannot route between two diagrams?
questions_used.answer: The OOB LAN node is drawn a second time, inside the in-band diagram, as an explicit boundary stub carrying the same group tag (so the same hue), and its single edge reaches NVOS. The planes stay separate — the sections are separated by blank space and a rule, never a box — and the relation is not dropped.
questions_used.reason: The engine namespaces diagram node ids and separates sections with a blank row and a rule, so a cross-diagram route is impossible. The frozen constraint set forbids dropping a relation, and 'oob -> nvos' is a source relation.

questions_used.question: Which verbs and protocols label the routes, when the frozen relation list says 'unlabeled — do not invent a protocol'?
questions_used.answer: Only what the excerpts state, on the route that states it: 'client' on rms -> oob ('It is a client on that network, not part of it'), 'Redfish/HTTPS' on the OOB trunk (the LAN carries Redfish over HTTPS), 'hosts' on nvos -> nmxc (NVOS hosting NMX-C/T), 'DaemonSet' on gpuop -> dcgm ('deployed as a DaemonSet by the GPU Operator'), ':9400' on dcgm -> dcgmx (the exporter's Prometheus port) and 'NVML' on dcgm -> drvk (reads GPU state via NVML against the driver). k8s -> gpuop and drvk -> fm stay unlabeled: no excerpt states a verb, and 'manages'/'deploys' would be the invented dependency the constraint forbids.
questions_used.reason: source.md gives the protocols in its excerpts; the label rule in the case is 'protocols where the excerpts give them', so using them is not inventing, and adding any other verb would be.

triage.converged_when: The reader's job (per component: which plane, which controller reaches it), the audited claims (nv-rms is a client of the OOB LAN; DCGM has no OOB edge), the shape (a canvas with one described diagram per world), the trunk (one corridor, one split, three destinations) and the free-software rule were all fixed by the framing and the annex answers; nothing else changes the drawing.
triage.shape_decision: canvas: 2 described diagrams — 'OOB hardware-control plane' (oob) and 'In-band compute and NVSwitch software' (inband)

classification.evidence: Two weakly-connected worlds — oob/rms/bmc_c/bmc_s/pwr on one side, k8s/gpuop/dcgm/dcgmx/drvk/fm/nvos/nmxc on the other — joined by exactly one bus (the OOB LAN, which fans to three device classes) and one cross-plane relation (oob -> nvos).
tie_breakers_considered: Density (E=11 vs N=13, so E < N): would favour flow-chains, but a chain has one relation per node and no shared bus — the OOB LAN has four, three of them through one declared trunk.
A bus between disconnected worlds means placement-planes, even when the bus looks like a chain (tie-breaker 2).
Identifier content: the case carries protocols and one port (:9400), but they are labels on a structural graph, not the subject — identity-probe-map (tie-breaker 3) does not win.
classification.secondary_recipe: identity-probe-maps habits borrowed for coverage only: every protocol/identifier the excerpts give (Redfish/HTTPS, NVML, :9400, DaemonSet, hosts, client) was made a ledger row before the spec, and qualified facts were kept as qualifiers (nv-rms source free, image gated) instead of being cleaned up.

view_shape.rung_chosen: rung 2 — one canvas hosting named, described concept-diagrams
source_facts_that_decided_it: The source's own task line separates four things (off-rack management, OOB hardware control, NVSwitch software, in-band compute software) and the brief's reader wants per-component plane membership: the picture is two worlds, not one graph.
The two worlds share exactly one relation (oob -> nvos), so they separate cleanly without losing a relation.

One view has to hold both worlds in a single layout: 13 nodes, 11 relations and 6 protocol/verb labels (up to 13 characters) whose gutters cost rank rows. Measured, the two worlds need different rank depths (3 ranks vs 5 ranks), so a single tb drawing takes the union depth and the label gutters push it past 47 rows; the two sections measured here are 58x38 and 32x49 on their own, and 95 rows together.
The triage annex answer 4 makes the reader's preference explicit: a canvas with a diagram per world is fine if the planes stay apart.

rejected_rungs.reason: 13 nodes with two weakly-connected worlds, a three-way trunk fan and 6 labels in a single layout cannot fit 77x47 at natural zoom without thinning relations or shrinking text: the two worlds have different rank depths (3 vs 5), so one drawing needs the union depth plus the label gutters, and the measured sections are 58x38 and 32x49 on their own (95 rows stacked).

rejected_rungs.rung: rung 3 — add a diagram rather than drop a concept
rejected_rungs.reason: No concept was dropped, so no extra diagram was needed. Splitting the in-band world further (compute vs NVSwitch software) was considered and rejected: the source names NVSwitch software as its own tier, but the brief places NVOS/NMX-C/T inside the in-band world, and a three-node section would be a fragment, not a concept.

residual_is_structural.demand: one trunk that splits once into three destinations, with no route inside the two-cell margin of a box it does not serve
residual_is_structural.why_it_cannot_be_met: The engine's hub junction is placed at the corridor cell nearest the branch centroid, which is always one to two rows above the middle box's top (router.rs try_hub: candidates sort by distance to the centroid of the branch centres). Both arms therefore leave that cell two rows above that box's span and cross it at ring 2. Routing cannot recover: the near-node price is NEAR_BAND_COST 8 against STEP_COST 10 per cell, so the A* only takes a detour when it is under one cell long. Every fan topology that keeps the corridor clean (terminus centred) puts the junction over the terminus; every topology that moves the junction off it puts the corridor in the three-cell sibling gap (probe-fan c) or beside the boxes (probe-fan b).
residual_is_structural.how_close_the_shipped_surface_comes: The bus itself — the part the round-11 a3 defect was about — is fully clear: 0 corridor cells, and the in-band world is at 0. The residual is 2 routes x one box.

self_assessment: Not green. The drawing covers all 13 nodes and all 11 relations, the trunk splits once at one junction, the trunk corridor and the whole in-band world route clear of unrelated boxes, and the planes, hues and descriptions are drawn as the brief asks. Two validator checks fail, both from the trunk's split arms; the measurements say no legal arrangement of this engine's trunk hub avoids them, and both are listed as defects above.
